nodes.description: A patent document titled "Social medical network for diagnosis assistance" describing a method for diagnosis assistance using similarity between medical cases and experts in a common embedding space.

nodes.entity_id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance
nodes.description: The title of the patent US9589231B2, referring to a network-based system for assisting medical diagnosis.
nodes.id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance

nodes.description: A method that exploits similarity between a new medical case and existing medical cases and experts embedded in a common embedding space to assist diagnosis.

A medical case submitted by a requester as part of a query, which is embedded in an embedding space for comparison with existing cases and experts.<SEP>A case for which a diagnosis is sought, comprising a plurality of records relating to a specific patient, such as laboratory test results, images, symptom descriptions, patient monitor results, diagnoses, and prescribed medications and treatments.

A set of previously recorded medical cases embedded in the embedding space, used as candidates for similarity-based retrieval.<SEP>A set of prior medical cases each having a multidimensional representation in the embedding space, used for comparison against a new case.

A set of medical experts embedded in the embedding space, who may be selected to provide a diagnosis for a new medical case.<SEP>A set of experts each embedded in the embedding space based on information such as expert profiles, coded medical procedures performed, authored articles, and linked stored medical cases; experts may be ranked by availability, rating, and number of followers.

A common space in which new medical cases, existing medical cases, and experts are embedded as multidimensional representations for similarity computation.<SEP>A multidimensional space in which new medical cases, existing medical cases, and experts are embedded as multidimensional representations.

The party submitting a query request including a new medical case and selecting a query type.<SEP>A user who submits a query request including a new medical case and selects from a plurality of query types.

A query type that returns a subset of existing medical cases based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.<SEP>A query type that returns a subset of existing cases based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.

A query type that returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.<SEP>A query type that returns a subset of experts based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts, and may provide the new case to a selected expert for formulating a diagnosis.

A computed cost for a query, differing between query-for-experts and query-for-cases, with the query-for-experts cost being higher.<SEP>A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts is different from (higher than) the cost for a query-for-cases.

A set of medical concepts joined by links, used to compute multidimensional representations of medical cases and experts, where each concept corresponds to a dimension.<SEP>An ontology that includes parts of the human body, biological functions, medical conditions, pharmacological substances, and combinations thereof, and may be based on the Unified Medical Language System.
Concepts in the medical ontology joined by links, each corresponding to a respective dimension in the representation.

A matrix applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology when computing similarity.<SEP>A matrix applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology.
A processor used to perform at least one of the embedding, providing, returning subsets, and computing query cost steps.
Parts of the human body included in the medical ontology.
Biological functions included in the medical ontology.
Medical conditions included in the medical ontology.
Pharmacological substances included in the medical ontology.
A medical ontology system on which the medical ontology used in the method is based.

A computation of similarity between the representation of the new case and representations of existing cases or experts, optionally applying a matrix of proximities that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology.

A system comprising memory storing instructions and a processor for executing them, used to receive query requests, embed new medical cases, return subsets of cases or experts, and compute query costs.
A set of devices in a network for linking requesters and experts with the diagnosis assistance system.
A network comprising a diagnosis assistance system and a set of user devices for linking requesters and experts with the system.
A product comprising a non-transitory recording medium storing instructions that, when executed on a computer, cause the computer to perform the diagnosis assistance method.
A payment made to an expert for formulating a diagnosis when the query-for-experts is selected.
A database from which documents are returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and documents embedded in the embedding space.
The diagnosis formulated by a selected expert to whom the new case is provided.

edges.description: The diagnosis assistance method receives a query request that includes a new medical case.
The diagnosis assistance method embeds the new medical case in an embedding space.
The method computes multidimensional representations of the medical case based on a medical ontology.
At least one of the method steps is performed with a computer processor.
The requester submits a query request including a new medical case.
The matrix of proximities is applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case to account for relationships between concepts in the ontology.
The new case may be communicated to a selected subset of experts for the expert to attempt to provide a diagnosis.
The new medical case is embedded in the embedding space.
The diagnosis assistance system receives a query request including a new medical case and embeds the new medical case in the embedding space.
The embedding space contains embedded representations of a set of existing medical cases.<SEP>The set of existing medical cases is embedded in the embedding space.

The query-for-cases returns a subset of existing medical cases based on computed similarity with the embedded new case.<SEP>When the query-for-cases is selected, a subset of the cases is returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.
The embedding space contains embedded representations of a set of experts.<SEP>The set of experts is embedded in the embedding space.

The query-for-experts returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity with the embedded new case.<SEP>When the query-for-experts is selected, a subset of the experts is returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.
The user devices link experts with the system.
Each medical concept corresponds to a respective dimension in the representation within the embedding space.
The requester may select the query-for-cases query type.
The requester may select the query-for-experts query type.
The requester submits a request for a query to the diagnosis assistance system.
The user devices link requesters with the system.
The query-for-cases is associated with a computed query cost lower than that of the query-for-experts.<SEP>The cost for a query-for-cases differs from the cost for a query-for-experts.
The diagnosis assistance system provides for the requester to select from query types including a query-for-cases.
When the query-for-cases is selected, documents from a public database are returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and documents embedded in the embedding space.
When the query-by-cases is selected, a query-by-experts may be performed subsequent to the query-by-cases.
The query-for-experts is associated with a higher computed query cost than the query-for-cases.<SEP>The cost for a query-for-experts is different from the cost for a query-for-cases.
When the query-for-experts is selected, the new case is provided to a selected expert for formulating a diagnosis.
When the query-for-experts is selected, provision is made for making a payment to the expert for formulating the diagnosis.
The diagnosis assistance system provides for the requester to select from query types including a query-for-experts.
The diagnosis assistance system computes a cost for the query.
The medical ontology comprises a set of medical concepts joined by links.
The ontology includes parts of the human body.
The ontology includes biological functions.
The ontology includes medical conditions.
The ontology includes pharmacological substances.
The medical ontology is based on the Unified Medical Language System.
The matrix of proximities accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology.
The similarity measure applies a matrix of proximities to the multidimensional representation of the new case.
The network comprises a system for diagnosis assistance.
The computer program product stores instructions that when executed cause a computer to perform the method of the diagnosis assistance system.
The network comprises a set of user devices for linking requesters and experts with the system.
